subtype: Approach: checking in halfway and reassigning slow tasks [Revision]
passage: Class teacher's note, Friday. Halfway through the week, Manjula stood at the front of her group and checked the chart. "Who has finished what?" Two boxes were empty: Aman's writing part. Aman had been ill on Monday and Tuesday. Manjula did not scold. "Aman, you take the labels. Jomon, can you write the first paragraph? Karan, the second." Aman looked relieved. On Friday afternoon the project was complete, and the group presented on time. I did not tell them what to do; I noticed how the group stopped, looked at the pending work and changed the plan while there was still time.

qa.q: What job did Manjula give Aman?
How might Aman have felt when the jobs were changed?
qa.a: Aman looked relieved; being ill had left the writing undone, and the easier job meant Aman did not have to catch up alone.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the group use, and why?
qa.a: They could ask the teacher to extend the deadline for the ill member. Sharing the work themselves was quicker, though, and let the project be finished on time.

qa.q: How might Jomon see being asked to write the first paragraph?
qa.a: Jomon may feel trusted with an important part, or maybe a little pressed for time, but the question was asked politely, so it was a fair request.

grounding: At the halfway check the group sees that an ill member's writing is unfinished, shares the ill member's paragraphs and gives an easier job so the project ends on time.

subtype: Approach: checking in halfway and reassigning slow tasks [Revision]
passage:
Wednesday
Halfway to the deadline, so I made our group show what we'd done so far. Drawings, done. Nisha's map, done. Gurpreet's part, the four paragraphs, not started. He'd had fever all last week and looked worried saying it. Instead of getting cross, we split his paragraphs: Nisha takes two, I take two. Gurpreet will stick everything on the chart and write the headings, which is easier. He looked so relieved and said, 'Thanks, Kunal.'
Friday
Finished! On time, even a day early. Gurpreet's headings are the neatest part of the whole chart.

qa.q: Why hadn't Gurpreet started his paragraphs?
qa.a: He'd had fever all last week.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel when the group shared out his paragraphs?
qa.a: He looked worried at first and then very relieved when the others took his paragraphs and gave him an easier job.

qa.q: What made the halfway check-in useful?
qa.a: It showed the missing paragraphs early, while there was still time to share them out and finish on time.

qa.q: How might Nisha see taking on two extra paragraphs?
qa.a: Nisha agreed to take two, so Nisha probably saw it as fair help for someone who had been ill.

grounding: Shows a group checking in halfway, finding an ill member's writing undone, sharing his paragraphs and giving him an easier job so they finish on time.

subtype: Approach: checking in halfway and reassigning slow tasks [Revision]
passage: Halfway through the week, Tanuja gathered her group under the neem tree behind the school. 'Let's see where we are.' Pinki's drawings were done. Tanuja's map of their block was done. Suraj's writing about the local crops had only two lines. He'd been sick with a cough for four days, and he kept his eyes on the ground. Tanuja thought for a moment. 'Pinki and I will each write one of your parts. You colour the map borders and paste the photos. Okay?' Suraj looked up. 'Okay.' On Saturday the chart was pinned on the classroom wall, a day before the deadline, with Suraj's neat borders around every village.

qa.q: Where did Tanuja gather her group?
qa.a: Under the neem tree behind the school.

qa.q: How did Suraj seem to feel before Tanuja's plan?
qa.a: He kept his eyes on the ground, so he seemed embarrassed and worried about his unfinished part.

qa.q: What else could the group do to catch problems earlier next time?
qa.a: Check in at a set point every week; the halfway check is what let them reshare the work and still finish early.

qa.q: How did the new plan change things for Suraj?
qa.a: Suraj got a job he could manage after being ill, colouring borders, and his neat work ended up on the finished chart.

grounding: Illustrates a group checking progress midway, sharing out an ill member's unwritten part and giving him an easier task, so the project is finished in time.
